messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@carehub.com>, Elizabeth Hayes <elizabeth.hayes@carehub.com>

Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: HIPAA scope & hosting options — CareHub discovery

Hi Michael / Elizabeth —

Thanks again for a constructive call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary from our call:
- Primary ask: confirm where PHI will be sent to Redwood and what classes of PHI (e.g., patient identifiers, clinician notes, device telemetry) are in scope.
- Compliance checks: you asked about our SOC 2 status, encryption at rest/in transit, and BAA availability.
- Hosting options discussed: (1) Redwood Hosted API with controlled redaction & tokenization, (2) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), (3) Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem).

Immediate actions we propose:
1) I attached a short security questionnaire (CareHub_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf) — please complete or highlight any sections you want us to pre-fill.
2) Confirm PHI classes in-scope and an estimate of daily token volumes so we can size Dedicated/private options.
3) We’ll attach a SOC 2 summary and a high-level architecture note for each hosting option (see SOC2-TypeII-summary-2026.pdf).
4) If BAA is required, our legal team can start a draft once we have a basic LOI / letter of intent — typical timeline for BAA review + signature is 1–2 weeks after LOI depending on redlines.

Notes on architecture tradeoffs (very high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to start, supports redaction/tokenization pipelines but not suitable if you need full-network isolation and strict on-prem requirements.
- Dedicated: predictable throughput and data isolation inside a reserved pool; supports stricter logging and retention controls.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): required for many regulated workflows — longer lead time (~4–6 weeks) and procurement steps.

Proposed owners & timing:
- CareHub: complete the questionnaire (Michael / Elizabeth) — target EOW (Fri Sep 18)
- Redwood (Sofia / Marissa / Neha): return completed SOC2 summary and hosting architecture notes by Wed Sep 17
- Redwood legal (Karthik): prepare BAA draft after LOI — target timeline 1–2 weeks post-LOI

Would you confirm the PHI classes and whether a hosted+tokenization approach is acceptable as an interim step while we coordinate a Dedicated/Private timeline?

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: HIPAA scope & hosting options — CareHub discovery

Thanks Sofia — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) PHI in scope: primarily patient identifiers (name, DOB, MRN), clinical notes (unstructured text), and limited device telemetry (heart rate, basic sensor readings). We do not intend to send imaging or raw audio at this stage.

2) Interim approach: our security team prefers not to send full PHI to third-party hosted APIs until a BAA is signed. Would Redwood support an approach where we send tokenized IDs (CareHub-managed tokenization) and redacted clinical snippets to the Hosted API while the BAA/legal review proceeds?

3) SOC 2: can you confirm whether Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report covers hosting environment (control environment) and encryption key management? An executive summary would be helpful for our security team.

4) Timeline: we will start filling the questionnaire this afternoon; legal will loop in our procurement counsel for BAA discussion. Expect a response on the questionnaire by Sep 18 end of day.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Michael
Michael Torres
Director of Security Operations | CareHub Health

Subject: Re: Follow-up: HIPAA scope & hosting options — CareHub discovery

Hi Michael / Elizabeth —

Quick answers to your questions and proposed next steps from Redwood's side: 

SOC 2: Redwood completed a SOC 2 Type II audit in Nov 2025. The attached "SOC2-TypeII-summary-2026.pdf" is a redacted executive summary that highlights scope (infrastructure + service org controls), encryption, and key management practices. We can provide the full report under NDA if needed — let us know and we'll route through security.

Hosted API + tokenization: Yes, we support an interim model where CareHub retains tokenization on your side and Redwood only receives tokenized identifiers and redacted snippets. This reduces PHI exposure while legal reviews the BAA. A few implementation notes:
- We recommend tokenization at the edge (CareHub) and passing a mapping key via a secured lookup if you plan to rehydrate internally.
- We can add an extra verification layer in our ingestion pipeline (whitelisting of token prefixes) and strict logging/retention policies for those requests.

Deployment options and rough timelines:
- Hosted API (with tokenization): fastest — can be done within days after questionnaire clarifications and ACL setup.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): 2–3 weeks to provision and baseline testing once volumes are confirmed.
- Private (VPC): 4–6 weeks, depends on network provisioning and legal/ops procurement.

Next steps (owners):
1) CareHub: return questionnaire and confirm PHI classes (Michael / Elizabeth) — target Sep 18 EOD.
2) Redwood: provide tech-design note for tokenization flows and a checklist for Dedicated/Private prerequisites (Sofia / Neha) — target Sep 17.
3) Redwood legal: prepare BAA draft on receipt of LOI or written confirmation of intent (Karthik) — target 1–2 weeks post-LOI.

If useful, we can schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough next week to align on token format and ingestion controls. Sofia, can you propose 2x slots?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
